issues.issue: "Witnesses for the accused may be called" is permissive, which sits against 23.C.2's statement of a right "to present witnesses on their own behalf" and 19.9's rule that testimony "may be disallowed" if a witness is not available when called. Whether the accused has a right or only a possibility of calling witnesses depends on reading the three together.

This footnote says hearing procedures "may differ" in sexual misconduct, sexual harassment, and sex discrimination cases "in accordance with Title IX" without stating how, which cannot be squared with the mandatory step-by-step procedure of Section 23 or the specific Section 3 and 7 rules in 19.13, 19.16 and 19.17. In the successor handbook such cases are removed from Section 19 entirely and sent to the Special Examiner's Process, so the footnote is the only textual hook for wholly different procedures.
"Usually within 3-5 business days" promises notification without fixing any deadline, and notice is by Brandeis e-mail only. The word "usually" makes the timing unenforceable.

The Board hears the accuser's sanction recommendation, though Section 21.0 assigns the sanctioning judgment to the DSRCS administrator or the SCB on stated factors and 19.13 has the Board recommend the sanction. The weight, if any, to be given the accuser's recommendation is unstated.

Final sanction determinations go to the accused "and in some cases to the accuser," which cannot be squared with the Section 3 services statement that "the accuser will be informed of the outcome of disciplinary proceedings in which sexual assault is alleged." One provision makes notice to the accuser discretionary, the other absolute.

The Hearing Administrator's disclosure of the accused's past conduct during deliberations cannot be squared with 19.13's requirement that "Decisions shall be based solely upon evidence and testimony introduced at the hearing," nor with 19.6's statement that the administrator will not act in any way to influence the outcome. Whether the bar applies only to the responsibility finding or also to sanctioning is left unanswered.

"The appropriate administrator" who reviews the Board's recommendations is unidentified here, while 21.1 names the Director or Associate Dean and, for suspension or dismissal, the Dean. Which officer reviews, and with what power to modify, must be assembled from other provisions.

Appeal procedures are relegated to "the nal outcome letter," a document outside the handbook, even though 19.16 already prescribes the grounds and the 7-day deadline. If the letter and 19.16 differ, nothing says which controls.
